claims.text: High configurational entropy competes with favorable atomic pair interactions in high-entropy nanoalloys.
Favorable interactions between specific elemental pairs drive the development of local chemical short-range order.
Local chemical order suppresses diffusional phase separation.
The balance between configurational entropy and pair-interaction-driven local order governs structural and chemical stability.
The proposed starting material is a well-mixed, near-equiatomic, disordered single-phase nanoalloy.
Annealing at approximately 700–1200 °C under an inert or reducing atmosphere is the proposed intervention.
A controlled inert or reducing atmosphere minimizes oxidation during high-temperature annealing.
At high temperature, configurational entropy stabilizes a disordered solid solution.
Thermally enabled atomic mobility allows favorable pair interactions to initiate local ordering.
Favorable pair interactions lower the local free energy.
Emergent short-range chemical order acts as a barrier to diffusion.
The diffusion barrier created by short-range order suppresses phase segregation and preserves nanostructural integrity.
Annealed samples will exhibit more local chemical order than baseline samples maintained in a disordered state.
Annealed samples with enhanced local order will resist phase separation and microstructural degradation better than the baseline.
The prediction is expected to apply to nanoalloys containing multiple refractory or strongly interacting elements.
The stabilizing effect should diminish in alloys lacking favorable specific pair interactions.
The predicted effect may diminish under oxidizing conditions.

Local order can be quantified by atom probe tomography or pair-distribution analysis, while phase segregation and structural integrity can be assessed by X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy.

contradictions.description: The intervention is only high-temperature annealing, while one baseline is described as being held at the same temperature without an additional ordering-promoting step that is never defined. Elsewhere the baseline may receive no treatment at all. Thus the control is inconsistently specified and may either be indistinguishable from the intervention or differ in thermal exposure.

The baseline alternates between a high-temperature-treated sample that remains disordered and an untreated sample, so the proposed comparison does not consistently isolate local ordering from annealing history.
